audit.whatIsWrong: The entry describes a "Q root" five times — spikes[1], wants.foe[0], mid, whys[0], whys[3] all have Aurora rooting Tahm Kench with her Q.
audit.why: Twofold Hex applies no crowd control at all. Riot's text: "sends out a missile that curses any enemies it hits. She can then recast the ability to draw active curses back toward herself, damaging foes who are hit along the way." Its only flag is projectile. This is a fabricated root, and it is the most dangerous kind of error in the file: a Tahm Kench who believes he will be rooted will refuse approaches that are actually free, and will hold Flash for a CC that never comes.
audit.corrected: Twofold Hex chips and curses; it does not root. The only hard CC in her kit is Between Worlds (R).
sources: champ-data/_kits/aurora.json (Q: Twofold Hex, flags: projectile only; R: Between Worlds, flags include hardCC)

audit.whatIsWrong: The entry consistently calls E "her blink" and has it stepping her IN — spikes[1] "Her E blink lets her freely step into cast range", mid "Her E blink lets her step in", wants.foe[0] "Use E blink".
audit.why: Her W and E are swapped. Across the Veil (W) is the leap that closes or repositions and grants invisibility, on 22/21/20/19/18. The Weirding (E) damages and slows and then hops her BACKWARD only, on 15/14/13/12/11. E cannot step her in. Getting these the wrong way round means the reader tracks the wrong cooldown before committing — and the two differ by seven seconds at rank 1.
audit.corrected: Across the Veil is the gap-closer and the vanish; The Weirding is the poke-and-retreat.
sources: champ-data/_kits/aurora.json (W: "leaps in a direction, entering the spirit realm upon landing, becoming invisible", cd 22/21/20/19/18; E: "damages and slows enemies before Aurora hops backward to safety", cd 15/14/13/12/11)

audit.whatIsWrong: wants.foe[2] says "Build up W spirit form to exile herself" and whys[4] calls it "W spirit exile" that "removes her from your Devour window".
audit.why: The conclusion is right but the mechanism is wrong, and the mechanism is what a player acts on. W is a single 22s cast, not something built up, and it grants INVISIBILITY rather than untargetability or an exile. It denies Devour because Devour is point-and-click and you cannot click what you cannot see — which also tells you the counterplay: control wards and lane brush vision, not damage.
audit.corrected: Across the Veil makes her invisible for a short window on 22s; Devour is point-and-click and will not cast on an unseen target.
sources: League of Legends Wiki — Tahm Kench (wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Tahm_Kench) — Devour cast range 250, requires 3 stacks

audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer names Aurora's matchup-defining ability "Twofold Hunt" in tldr, winCon, enemyWin, breakdown.cooldowns, breakdown.trading, dosFull[0].t, dosFull[0].d, phases[1].why, phases[3].why and phases[5].why, and describes it as "Her escape" and "Twofold Hunt (Blink)".
audit.why: Two errors stacked. The name is wrong — her Q is Twofold Hex, not Twofold Hunt. And the role is wrong — Twofold Hex is a poke missile, not a blink or an escape. The ability the full layer is actually describing is Across the Veil. As with Ambessa, suspectNames did not catch this because it only scans the content layer.
audit.corrected: The ability to track before committing is Across the Veil, 22s at rank 1.
sources: champ-data/_kits/aurora.json (Q: Twofold Hex; W: Across the Veil)

audit.whatIsWrong: Between Worlds is never mentioned anywhere in the entry, even though the level-6 stage is handed to Aurora.
audit.why: The stage text at 6 talks about her W instead. Between Worlds is 140s at rank 1 and creates a slowing zone she can teleport across — that is what changes the level-6 geometry, and it is also the longest cooldown in her kit, so it is the biggest punish window on the map.
audit.corrected: Named at the level-6 stage with its cooldown and its actual effect.
sources: champ-data/_kits/aurora.json (R: Between Worlds, cd 140/120/100, "creates an area that slows enemies within it and allows Aurora to teleport from one side of the area to the other")

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[2], wants.you[2], mid, late and whys[5] all build the level-6 plan around "Abyssal Voyage".
audit.why: Abyssal Voyage is the removed pre-rework ultimate. Abyssal Dive is the current W — a blink available from level 2 that knocks up on arrival, on 21/20/19/18/17. Against a champion whose whole plan is holding spacing, that distinction matters enormously: the blink is a gap-closer you have had since level 2, not a level-6 escape.
audit.corrected: Abyssal Dive, live from level 2, used to close the gap she maintains rather than to run away at 6.
sources: League of Legends Wiki — Tahm Kench (wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Tahm_Kench)

audit.whatIsWrong: No anti-heal recommendation anywhere, despite Aurora healing continuously.
audit.why: Spirit Abjuration heals her from spirits exorcised by every spell and attack she lands. In a poke lane where she is landing Twofold Hex on cooldown, that healing is what turns your chip damage into a losing exchange. This one is a genuine anti-heal case, unlike the false positive flagged for Ambessa.
audit.corrected: Grievous Wounds folded into the stacking plan in wants.you[0].
sources: champ-data/_kits/aurora.json (P: "Exorcised spirits follow Aurora around and heal her")

audit.whatIsWrong: early promises "If you land the three-stack stun... you can Devour her".
audit.why: The Q stun at 3 stacks consumes all three stacks and Devour requires 3 stacks. The one clean kill window this losing lane offers is described as a combo that cannot be executed.
audit.corrected: Reach three stacks and spend them on the eat directly — the stun consumes the same three.
sources: League of Legends Wiki — Tahm Kench (wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Tahm_Kench)

audit.why: The content-layer chart handing Aurora levels 4-6 and returning the lane at two items is a fair read of a 47.85% matchup over 535 games — Tahm Kench loses the poke phase and wins on scaling. Note however that full.diff is "EVEN" at 6/10 here, which understates a losing lane; same length-band problem as the Aatrox entry, so no edit proposed.

edits.before: You have the early edge but it is narrow. Tongue Lash's range and slow lets you contest the wave and begin stacking An Acquired Taste without walking into melee range, and Aurora at levels 1-2 has no answer to a stun if she stands still. The priority is to land Tongue Lash at max range — not to chase — and let the slow do the work of pulling her into a second auto. If you land the three-stack stun before she hits level 3 and gets her blink, you can Devour her and erase a full wave of CS. Accept that she will space backward after each exchange; you are setting up the stun window, not running her down.
edits.after: You have the early edge but it is narrow. Tongue Lash's 900 range and slow lets you contest the wave and begin stacking An Acquired Taste without walking into melee range, and Aurora at levels 1-2 has no answer if she stands still. The priority is to land Tongue Lash at max range — not to chase — and let the slow do the work of pulling her into a second auto. Reach three stacks before Across the Veil is available and you can Devour her outright; spend them on the eat, because the Q stun consumes the same three. Accept that she will space backward after each exchange; you are setting up that one window, not running her down.

edits.before: This is where Aurora takes control of the matchup. Her E blink lets her step in, fire Q-root poke, and immediately disengage before you can stack An Acquired Taste to three — she is actively resetting your stack count every trade. Do not burn Flash trying to gap-close; you will miss the stun and she will blink out, leaving you down a summoner. Play the wave, fish Tongue Lash from max range hoping she missteps, and activate Thick Skin the instant you break combat to convert grey health before her next poke cycle comes back up. Level 6 Abyssal Voyage is your pressure relief valve — use it to reposition away from her preferred spacing and force her to recalculate rather than standing still and eating her poke rhythm.
edits.after: This is where Aurora takes control of the matchup. Across the Veil leaps her in, Twofold Hex curses you for the poke, and The Weirding hops her straight back out before you can stack An Acquired Taste to three — she resets your stack count every trade. Neither ability roots you, so do not play as though you are held in place; the danger here is the chip, not the lockdown. Do not burn Flash trying to gap-close; you will miss and she will vanish, leaving you down a summoner. Fish Tongue Lash from max range, and activate Thick Skin the instant you break combat to convert grey health before her next poke cycle returns. At 6 Between Worlds gives her a slowing zone she can teleport across, so pick your angle before she places it.

edits.before: At two items you become the matchup's problem. Thick Skin backed by Heartsteel or Sunfire means Aurora's burst does not kill you before grey health converts and you have a second health bar to trade through — you become the threat she must disengage from rather than the target she can freely poke. Your job is to anchor teamfights, absorb her burst, and force her to burn E blink offensively so your carries can follow up. She still outpokes you in a straight lane if you let her pick her range, so never give her a static target — Abyssal Voyage repositioning keeps her honest and your team alive.
edits.after: At two items you become the matchup's problem. Thick Skin backed by Heartsteel or Sunfire means Aurora's burst does not kill you before grey health converts and you have a second health bar to trade through — you become the threat she must disengage from rather than the target she can freely poke. Your job is to anchor teamfights, absorb her burst, and force Across the Veil out defensively so your carries can follow up. She still outpokes you in a straight lane if you let her pick her range, so never stand still — and hold your three stacks until she is visible and inside 250.

notes:
This is the weakest entry in my slice and it got the most work. It contained a fabricated crowd-control effect: five separate strings describe Aurora rooting you with her Q. Twofold Hex has no CC of any kind. A player told to expect a root will misplay the approach in both directions — refusing free walk-ups and holding Flash for lockdown that never arrives.

Her W and E were also swapped throughout. Across the Veil (W, 22s) is the leap and the invisibility; The Weirding (E, 15s) damages, slows and hops her backward only. The entry had E doing the stepping-in. Seven seconds of cooldown difference at rank 1, so tracking the wrong one is a real cost.

SECOND FABRICATED FULL-LAYER ABILITY NAME: like Ambessa's "Repeating Dashes", the full layer here invents "Twofold Hunt" and additionally assigns it the wrong role ("Her escape", "Twofold Hunt (Blink)"). Two of the five matchups I have audited so far have a made-up ability name in the full layer. Since suspectNames only scans champ-data/content/*.js, the full layer has never been name-checked anywhere on the site. I would treat that as the highest-priority follow-up beyond this run.

Between Worlds (her R) was not mentioned anywhere in the entry despite the chart handing her the level-6 stage. I added it.

The anti-heal case here is genuine — Spirit Abjuration heals off every spell she lands — in contrast to the spurious anti-heal flag I rejected for Ambessa.
